subject.title: feat(plugin-sdk): propose CLI backend auth-forwarding contract

question: Should raw auth-profile material re-enter a public CLI-backend callback after security hardening removed it from `prepareExecution`, or must providers expose only a closed minimal bridge envelope?
rationale: The patch's mismatch defect is mechanical, but the permanent data-minimization and public-API boundary controls sensitive credentials and cannot be inferred safely without owner intent.

options.title: Keep profiles provider-owned
options.body: Validate selection inside the provider boundary and return only a closed minimal envelope to the CLI backend; review the complete seam before publishing it.

options.title: Permit controlled raw access
options.body: Allow selected raw profile fields through a new public resolver contract, with explicit security approval and complete compatibility, documentation, and upgrade proof.

recommendation.title: Keep profiles provider-owned
recommendation.body: Validate selection inside the provider boundary and return only a closed minimal envelope to the CLI backend; review the complete seam before publishing it.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced and hardened the canonical CLI auth bridge, making him the strongest feature-history owner for whether that credential boundary should be reopened.
